question: Does the unchanged default M5 observation/evaluation path still reproduce the full historical offline Genesis summary after the P26 adapter additions?
hypothesis: An additive recorded-track input method should leave every historical default-path cohort and reported metric unchanged.

sources.sections: _setup, _offline_episode and offline aggregation, read in full
sources.consequence: Use the historical CPU model factory, every-eighth-frame cohort, visibility/range filter, nearest-slot match and all waiting/kind breakdowns exactly.

sources.sections: make_model objects branch and ObjectModel.__init__ device selection
sources.consequence: The evaluator documents CPU execution, but its factory defaults to GPU when visible. Explicitly hide CUDA/HIP for this CPU reference regression; no new training moves to CPU.
Require exact cohort counts/keys and compare the published rounded errors at an absolute 1e-4 tolerance; numerical regression is distinct from new model efficacy.
Set one intra-op thread per worker before model work; use two CPU workers while the original GPU trainers continue.

differences: This is a complete legacy CPU reference regression on the original 400-unit export, not the new matched 100-unit P26 scientific comparison. The earlier D001 three-window equality check is insufficient to establish this aggregate invariant.
contrary_evidence: Unchanged high-level code can still produce drift through input data, imported functions, dependency versions or cohort selection. Preserve any discrepancy and investigate before claiming backward compatibility.

protocol.checks: all nested keys and counts exactly equal; every reported model/velocity/frozen median within absolute 1e-4; finite numeric values
protocol.provenance: hash every original metadata/data file, M5 checkpoint, historical summary and evaluated source

success: The full reference summary reproduces within the declared reporting precision; this does not establish the new P26 model-performance bars.
stop: No new simulation, training, checkpoint selection or modification of historical files. A mismatch is a technical regression requiring literature/source review before interpretation.
